column4: Top-down orthographic view of the keypad deck of a beige 1980s push-button desk telephone, filling the whole frame edge to edge: twelve square grey rubber number keys in a grid of three columns and four rows with small printed digits 1 to 9, star, 0 and hash, a small grey-green LCD strip across the top above them with a tiny red button beside it, on worn yellowed beige plastic. Pixel-art texture in the style of 1990s Build-engine games: chunky pixels, limited muted palette, flat even lighting, no perspective, no background, no other text.

Pixel-art game icon in the style of 1990s Build-engine games (Duke Nukem 3D, Redneck Rampage): chunky visible pixels, a limited muted palette, strong simple shading, a single old pear-shaped glass light bulb standing upright with a broken dark filament and a crack across the glass, its brass screw base at the bottom, a small amber warning glow round it, the object in the centre, filling the frame. Background must be flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF everywhere around it, no ground, no shadow, no text.
